Another logical argument for the existence of God is the "Argument of Improbability". Current science says the Big Bang exploded randomly and all the atoms just scattered without intention and from there the particles were governed by blind laws including Entropy. But if atoms tend to move toward chaos (entropy, 2nd law of thermodynamics), then how did the planets come together, how did life begin, where does our survival instinct come from? It's all random and has no cause?

The common analogy is the "Boeing 747 in a Hurricane" thought experiment: Imagine that there is disassembled Boeing 747 laying in a parking lot (all the pieces and metal laid out on the ground). And now a hurricane comes through and whips up everything into the air randomly, what are the odds that when the hurricane settles that a perfectly assembled Boeing 747 will be standing there and not just a random mess? The odds of life forming randomly has even farther odds than that.

This does not mean a conscious God created us knowingly. It simply suggests that there may be some principle that governs atoms in the direction of Chaos/disorder > Conscious structures/order. We already accept the principle of Entropy (the tendency for things to go from order to disorder) but our current scientific paradigm has no concept for the principle of Entelechy (the tendency for things to go from disorder to order, ie Living things).
